findings.reason: decimal.js:4344-4353 strips the sign before parseOther runs, so the error text does lose the sign. The existing '-' branch has always worked the same way, so the new '+' branch just follows the established idiom. No test or spec pins the error text, so this is not a defect of this change.
findings.claim: Stripping the leading '+' before validation means the error message shows the altered input.
findings.evidence: 'if (i === 43) v = v.slice(1);' runs before 'isDecimal.test(v) ? parseDecimal(x, v) : parseOther(x, v)', and parseOther throws 'Error(invalidArgument + str)' on the already-stripped string. So new Decimal('+-1') throws '[DecimalError] Invalid argument: -1', which names a valid number. The '-' branch already behaved this way, and T.assertException in test/setup.js only checks for /DecimalError/, so no test pins the message.
